    """
    Optimized hierarchical bucketing using pre-concatenation and view slicing:
    - Pre-concatenate all 48 tensors once into a single flat buffer
    - Use slices/views to select sub-buckets for all_reduce (no copy)
    - Use slices/views to unpack results (no copy)

    """
    # Pre-concatenate all gradients once
    all_flat = torch.cat([t.reshape(-1) for t in grads])
    
    # Compute offsets for each gradient in the flat buffer
    offsets = [0]
    for t in grads:
        offsets.append(offsets[-1] + t.numel())
    
    # Prepare output buffer (same size as input)
    out_flat = torch.zeros_like(all_flat)
    
    # Process in hierarchical buckets
    coarse_group_size = 12
    num_coarse_groups = 4
    sub_bucket_size = 4
    num_sub_buckets = 3
    
    for coarse_idx in range(num_coarse_groups):
        coarse_start_idx = coarse_idx * coarse_group_size
        
        for sub_idx in range(num_sub_buckets):
            # Calculate which tensors belong to this sub-bucket
            sub_start_idx = coarse_start_idx + sub_idx * sub_bucket_size
            sub_end_idx = sub_start_idx + sub_bucket_size
            
            # Get byte offsets for this sub-bucket
            byte_start = offsets[sub_start_idx]
            byte_end = offsets[sub_end_idx]
            
            # Extract slice view (no copy)
            bucket_slice = all_flat[byte_start:byte_end]
            
            # Perform all_reduce
            reduced = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, bucket_slice)
            
            # Write back to output buffer (slice assignment)
            out_flat[byte_start:byte_end] = reduced
    
    # Unpack output buffer into original shapes using views
    outs = []
    for i, t in enumerate(grads):

        end = offsets[i + 1]
